nodes.description: Abatacept, a CTLA4-Ig fusion protein that blocks T-cell costimulation, is an emerging option for severe, refractory or deep morphea; about 80% of treated patients were responders at month 12 for cutaneous and musculoskeletal activity. Case-series and cohort evidence only.

evidence.snippet: approximately 80% of patients receiving abatacept were responders at month 12 in matters of both cutaneous and musculoskeletal activity

nodes.description: Trigger factors in genetically predisposed individuals provoke an immunologically driven release of pro-inflammatory cytokines and a dense dermal and subcutaneous infiltrate of activated T lymphocytes (predominantly CD4+ T-helper cells), with plasma cells and eosinophils, that characterizes the early, active inflammatory phase. An interferon-gamma / CXCL9-CXCL10 gene signature in this phase correlates with clinical disease activity in juvenile morphea.

evidence.reference_title: Cytokine profiles in localized scleroderma and relationship to clinical features.
evidence.snippet: Histologically, a dense dermal and subcutaneous lymphocytic infiltrate is identified during this stage

evidence.reference_title: Cytokine profiles in localized scleroderma and relationship to clinical features.
evidence.snippet: both demonstrate a predominant CD4+ T-helper (Th) lymphocytic infiltrate
a large number of mononuclear lymphocytes (primarily activated T lymphocytes but also macrophages), some plasma cells and eosinophils infiltrate the skin and surrounding blood vessels
chemokine (C-X-C motif) ligand (CXCL)-9, CXCL-10, CXCL-11 and IFN-γ itself in correlation with the clinical disease activity
Symmetrical, hyperpigmented, round, slightly depressed and sharply demarcated plaques with varying diameters, from millimeters to several centimeters, are characteristic

nodes.description: A Th2-skewed cytokine milieu, in which TGF-beta and IL-4 predominate in the later fibrotic stage, activates dermal fibroblasts and drives their differentiation toward a collagen-producing myofibroblast phenotype.
nodes.id: Dermal Fibroblast Activation by TGF-beta and IL-4

evidence.snippet: the imbalance between Th1/Th2/Th17 cell subsets drives inflammation in the early stages of disease (Th1 and Th17 predominant) and fibrosis in the later stages of scleroderma (Th2 predominant)
In vitro experiments have shown that tissue fibrosis is caused by overshooting TGF-β and IL-4 activity

nodes.description: Over months to years the lesion becomes less inflammatory and more atrophic: thinned epidermis, dense dermal collagen, and loss of adnexal (eccrine, hair, sebaceous) structures, giving fine wrinkled dyspigmented skin and, in deeper forms, loss of subcutaneous tissue.
nodes.id: Dermal and Subcutaneous Sclerosis with Adnexal Atrophy

evidence.snippet: lesions become less sclerotic and more atrophic, showing a fine, wrinkled skin with dyspigmentation and loss of skin appendages

nodes.description: In genetically predisposed individuals, infections (including Borrelia burgdorferi, EBV and varicella zoster virus), local trauma or surgery, radiation and BCG vaccination are proposed triggers of the T-cell-driven skin inflammation that initiates morphea. No single exposure is established as causal.

evidence.snippet: various exogenous triggers are suggested, including some infections as for SSc, Epstein–Barr virus, varicella zoster virus and Borrelia burgdorferi, as well as local trauma, surgical operations, radiation and BCG vaccinations

nodes.description: TGF-beta drives synthesis of collagens, fibronectin and other extracellular-matrix proteins while suppressing collagenase, producing the densely packed homogeneous collagen that defines the sclerotic ("damage") phase.

evidence.snippet: TGF-β induces mitogenic activity in fibroblasts by matrix metalloproteinase (MMP)-3 and platelet-derived growth factor (PDGF) as well as the synthesis of several extracellular matrix proteins, such as collagens, fibronectin and others
they may lead to severe disfigurement (residual hyperpigmentation and skin atrophy), functional disability (joint contractures) and neuro-ophthalmologic complications

atrophy, loss of subcutaneous tissue and hypo- or hyper-pigmentation

nodes.description: Methotrexate, alone or with systemic corticosteroids, is first-line for moderate-to-severe, deep, linear or generalized morphea, and was superior to prednisone in a randomized controlled trial in children.

evidence.snippet: it was shown that methotrexate was superior to prednisone in matters of decrease in computerized skin score rates, development of new lesions and thermography findings at month 12

nodes.description: Mycophenolate mofetil is reserved for disease refractory or intolerant to methotrexate, or relapsing severe cases.

evidence.snippet: Mycophenolate mofetil is reserved for patients that are refractory, intolerant or with contraindications to methotrexate and/or relapsing, severe cases

nodes.description: Systemic corticosteroids are commonly combined with methotrexate for active deep, linear or generalized morphea.

evidence.snippet: methotrexate alone or in combination with systemic corticosteroids in more severe disease that additionally affects extracutaneous structures

nodes.description: The JAK1/JAK3 inhibitor tofacitinib improved clinical and histological skin thickness and joint mobility in case series of refractory, generalized morphea; it targets the JAK/STAT pathway downstream of the IFN-gamma signature seen in the active infiltrate. Case-series evidence only.

evidence.snippet: tofacitinib, a JAK1 and JAK3 inhibitor, led to improvement in both clinical and histological skin thickness and also joint mobility in numerous cases of refractory, generalized morphea

nodes.description: Topical calcipotriol/calcipotriene 0.005% ointment, alone or with phototherapy, for active plaque-type and linear morphea, particularly in children or disease refractory to topical corticosteroids.

evidence.snippet: Topical calcipotriene 0.005% and calcipotriol 0.005% ointments applied twice daily for 3 months, either alone or in combination with phototherapy represent a good therapeutic option for active, plaque-type and linear variants

nodes.description: Moderate-to-high-potency topical corticosteroids are used for active, limited (plaque-type) morphea; first-line for skin-restricted disease.

evidence.snippet: Topical corticosteroids of moderate to high potency are used for active, limited types of morphea

nodes.description: Topical tacrolimus 0.1% ointment for active, plaque-type morphea; a double-blind placebo-controlled pilot study showed improvement in clinical scores and skin hardness.

evidence.snippet: Tacrolimus 0.1% ointment may also be used in active, plaque-type morphea

nodes.description: Ultraviolet A1 phototherapy has the most robust evidence for morphea restricted to the skin.

evidence.snippet: the most robust data is available for ultraviolet A1 phototherapy in disease that is restricted to the skin, and methotrexate alone or in combination with systemic corticosteroids in more severe disease that additionally affects extracutaneous structures

nodes.description: The inflammatory phase begins with injury to the dermal vascular endothelium and upregulation of adhesion molecules (E-selectin, VCAM-1) that promote monocyte and lymphocyte adhesion and recruitment into the dermis — the earliest recognised step of the morphea cascade.

evidence.snippet: Up-regulation of several adhesion molecules, such as soluble E-selectin and soluble vascular adhesion molecule-1 (sVCAM-1) was observed in sera of morphea patients
